what_happened: In job 7z2t, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a request for a reconcile job over the athena/records branch, before work went on. The reading left the walk unbounded. The user bounded it. Commits before the first landing-intent record on athena/records are never reconciled, because the existing history check judges them until the cutover. When the records branch is missing or holds no intent, reconcile does nothing and says so. The user also asked for a test of that case.
cause: The reading is built from the request text alone. Nothing makes it say, for a process that walks history, where the walk starts, what it leaves to existing checks, and what it does when the input is absent or empty. During a migration the old and new mechanisms overlap, but the reading stage has no list of such cutover rules. Edge cases and boundaries therefore come in only when the user supplies them. The earlier case 0pna is similar: follow-up readings miss decisions that the user already holds.
prevention: Add a reading-stage requirement: for any criterion that walks history, records or a queue, the reading must state (1) the start boundary and which mechanism covers what lies before it, (2) the behavior when the source is absent or empty, and (3) a test criterion for each. Have the critic or reader reject a reading that lacks them. This applies to the whole class of unbounded-walk readings, including the reconcile case.
proposed_request: Add a reconcile job that walks commits against the landing records on athena/records. Bound the walk. Commits before the first landing-intent record on athena/records are never reconciled, and the existing history check judges them until the cutover. When the records branch is absent or holds no landing-intent record, reconcile changes nothing and prints a message saying there is nothing to reconcile. Add tests for both cases: commits before the first intent are skipped, and the branch is absent or has no intent.
